messages.subject: extracting time-frequency information from the spectro function
messages.subject_clean: extracting time-frequency information from the spectro function
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a time series of 13394 samples. When I use the spectro function it returns an object of 26 by 256 time-frequency samples. But when I look at the plot the time component of the spectogram looks much more detailed than just 26 time samples.

Is it possible to have the spectro function return much more time samples? I would like to have it return a time-frequency matrix of 13394 by 256 samples.

Thanks in advance,
  Robert

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] extracting time-frequency information from the spectro function
messages.subject_clean: [seewave] extracting time-frequency information from the spectro function
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

13394 samples / 512 = 26 FT windows. As the FT is a mirror function
you end up with 26 windows of 512/2 = 256 points.

If you want to increase the number of windows, use the argument 'ovlp'
that specifies the overlap between successive FT windows in %. For
isntance, a value of 50% will double the number of windows.

HTH

Jerome

messages.body_plain:
Hi, it is a non-sense to produce as many fft as the number of samples you have. By managing together the FFT size, the Window size (or the zero-padding parameter) and the overlap you can try to optimize the frequency-time resolution and selectivity according to the structure of your signal and the information you want to get.

Gianni

messages.subject: SAX's PAA Z-normalization?
messages.body_plain:
Hi. I'm looking at the algorithm for SAX in seewave's R package and the Z-normalization is not performed, as far as I can see.

The help page for SAX says (bolds are mine):
> SAX follows a two-step process: (1) Piecewise Aggregate Approximation (PAA) and (2) conversion a PAA sequence into a series of letters.
> PAA consists in a Z-normalisation, a segmentation of the series of length n into w segments, and the computation of each segment average.

Is this an oversight in the documentation or am I not seeing something that is indeed there? (I'm assuming Z-normalization results in a mean zero and a standard dev 1)

Thanks,

messages.subject: [seewave] Release of seewave 1.7.6
messages.body_plain:
Dear seewave users,

A new version of seewave (1.7.6) is on CRAN now.

New features:

o acoustat(): two new arguments, 'tlim' and 'flim' to control the time
and frequency limits of the analysis.

o akamatsu(): a new function to compute the resonance and cut frequency
in water tanks. By Camille Desjonqueres.

o diffcumspec(): a new function to compute dissimilarity between two
spectra based on the cumulative distribution functions. By Laurent Lellouch.

o fund(): a new argument, 'at', to estimate the fundamental frequency at
a specific position along the wave object.

o istft(): a new function to compute the inverse of the short-term
Fourier transform (ISTFT). Translated and adapted from a Matlab function
written by Hristo Zhivomirov.

o songmeter(): a new function to read and decompose the file name
produced by a SongMeter (Wildlife Acoustics (c)).

o spectro(): a new argument 'complex' to get the complex values of the
STFT when plot is FALSE.

o synth(): two new arguments 'signal' to control the signal function and
'partials' to produce harmonics. By Laurent Lellouch.

Thanks very much to Camill Desjonquères, Laurent Lellouch and Hristo
Zhivomirov for their contribution!

Enjoy,

Jerome

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] package 'seewave' is not available (for R version 3.1.1)
messages.subject_clean: [seewave] package 'seewave' is not available (for R version 3.1.1)
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I recently saw this problem with a Mac user in my lab. It is a dependencies problem. Seewave on Maverick returns the error "Package required but not available: ‘fftw’" (http://www.r-project.org/nosvn/R.check/r-release-osx-x86_64-mavericks/seewave-00check.html)

When you check why fftw fails, it says: "No package 'fftw3' found" (http://www.r-project.org/nosvn/R.check/r-release-osx-x86_64-mavericks/fftw-00check.html)

So, the problem is the fftw3 requirement. It is not installed in the machine CRAN is using, so the install fails.
Just install the libraries first (in OS X, not R), then you should be able to install fftw and seewave from the tar.gz files.

Luis J. Villanueva
http://research.CoquiPR.com
